html:
A Soviet physicist who helped design the Soviet hydrogen bomb and then became the country's best known dissident. He lived from 1921 to 1989 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1975.

In the late 1940s and 1950s he worked at a secret weapons centre. His design ideas were key to the first true Soviet thermonuclear bomb, tested in 1955, after the first Soviet atomic bomb in 1949. He was honoured as a hero of the state.

Growing worried about fallout from bomb tests, he pressed for a test ban. In 1968 he wrote an essay calling for peaceful coexistence, intellectual freedom and the meeting of the Soviet and Western systems. It was published abroad, and he lost his secret work. He spoke up for political prisoners and, with his wife Elena Bonner, became the conscience of the dissident movement.

After he condemned the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, he was exiled in 1980 to the closed city of Gorky. Mikhail Gorbachev freed him in 1986. He was elected to the new Soviet parliament in 1989 and died that December. The European Parliament's prize for freedom of thought bears his name.
sum: A Soviet physicist who helped design the Soviet hydrogen bomb and then became the country's best known dissident. He lived from 1921 to 1989 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1975.
